_note: What a coordinator needs to run, as data. `mas coordinator start` reads <state>/coordinator.json (written by `mas service install --role coordinator`, or by hand) and any flag given on the command line wins over the file; the file wins over these defaults. Knowledge lives here, not in Python. `type` is one of str, int, float, bool; `null_ok` lets a key be null.

bind.help: the address of the interface to listen on (loopback, private or link-local; never every interface)

port.help: the TCP port nodes connect to

discovery_port.help: the UDP port computers use to find this coordinator

no_discovery.help: do not open the discovery UDP socket

name.help: the name shown to computers that find this coordinator (default: the host name)

web.help: serve the owner's screen and the chat bridge on this computer only (loopback). A chat (Claude Desktop, Open WebUI) reaches this coordinator only while it is on

web_port.help: the loopback port of the web screen (0: any free one)

model_profile.help: the model profile the coordinator's agent uses (from the models file); without one analyses are code-only and say so

models_file.help: the models file (default: config/models.yaml of this program; a sibling models.local.yaml adds and overrides profiles)

include_virtual.help: also answer on VPN, container and virtual-machine interfaces

idle_timeout.help: seconds a connection may stay silent

board_escalation_limit.help: how many escalation steps a board may take without asking you first. A value outside 0 to the router's maximum (2) is clamped into that range. It counts steps, not money: a step to an API route spends your credit and there is no spend limit

_service_defaults_note: values a NEW coordinator.json gets when `mas service install` writes it and the owner did not say: a service has no terminal, so the chat bridge is on by default for it
